newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya dissident Koigi wa Wamwere freed on bail.
newsitem.headline: Kenya dissident Koigi wa Wamwere freed on bail.

text.p: Kenyan dissident Koigi wa Wamwere jailed for four years for robbery was freed on bail on Friday to seek medical treatment in South Africa or Europe, court officials said.

Kenyan Chief Justice Abdul Majid Cockar said he granted Wamwere's temporary liberty on medical and humanitarian grounds and: "It is my hope that the applicant would return to Kenya after undergoing treatment to face the appeal he has lodged."
Justice Cockar set bail at 200,000 shillings ($3,613).

Wamwere was admitted to the private Nairobi Hospital last month with cardiac complications. Kenyan cardiologists say he requires surgery to live. His lawyers say he will be admitted to a London hospital for an operation in January.
Wamwere and two others -- including his brother Charles Wamwere -- were jailed for four years in October 1995 for robbery. A fourth man was freed for lack of clear evidence.
They have appealed against the sentence, arguing that the magistrate erred in law. Under Kenyan laws, violent robbery is punishable by death, according to defence lawyer Paul Muite.
But the magistrate reduced the charge to plain robbery and handed the accused men prison terms, Muite argued.
The London-based human rights group Amnesty International has adopted Wamwere as a prisoner of conscience, saying that Kenyan authorities were punishing him for his political beliefs.
Wamwere is a former member of parliament for a constituency that includes President Daniel arap Moi's rural Kabarak home in his native Rift Valley province.

He was exiled in Norway between 1986 and 1990. He returned to Kenya under mysterious circumstances in 1990 and was charged in court with treason. Wamwere said at the time that Kenyan security forces had abducted him from neighbouring Uganda.
Koigi's wife and children still live in Norway. Norway has condemned Wamwere's conviction as a travesty of the justice.
